result.title: Time-Division Multiplexing: The Operational Rhythm and Temporal Organization Layer of Digital Life
result.summary: Continual agents must handle urgent interaction while retaining alternatives, replaying errors, and committing safe long-term changes. A previous digital-life framework distinguishes online (busy) and offline (idle) channels, but leaves open whether these are separate programs or phases of a common process and how their operations should be ordered. Motivated by recent observations of rapidly alternating perceptual representations in primate cortex, we develop a temporal organization layer with phase-tagged micro-epochs, an observable duty cycle, independent content and resource controls, and three nested clocks separating candidate exploration from durable commitment. We give a projected duty-cycle update, state its deterministic descent guarantee and the additional noise term required for a stochastic guarantee, and specify coupled busy/idle execution contracts. Five synthetic experiments (64 seeds each) examine descent and noise, objective misalignment, gain asymmetry, resource coupling, and dropped replay logs. In the gain/noise model the best tested gain ratio is 1.55; decoupled scheduling yields 26.6% versus 11.1% success on a constructed urgent/high-load subset. A frozen-backbone Qwen3-8B prototype further checks orchestration, but its proxy outcomes are not task-benchmark evidence. The results establish a testable scheduling design and identify its conditions of validity, not machine consciousness or general-purpose agent superiority.

AI.brief_summary: 论文提出一个“时间组织层”：以带相位标签的微时间片、可观测占空比与三层嵌套时钟，将代理的候选探索与长期承诺分开调度，并给出占空比更新的下降性保证、噪声项与 busy/idle 执行契约，配合五组合成实验及 Qwen3-8B 编排原型验证。
AI.relevance_reason: 其相位化时间片与嵌套时钟的调度契约，可能为 THINK/LOOK/STOP 的顺序编排与动态计算分配提供可核查的机制线索；但该工作面向通用持续代理且明确无任务基准证据，能否迁移到 latent 推理状态尚待确认。
